name: rnl-std-core
description:
rnl-std-core, the smallest collection of the standard package rnl-std (16.3): it references
rnl-std-style, rnl-std-symbols and rnl-std-virtual and has no content of its own. It draws the
netlist and adds nothing: the grounds, supplies and port tags for unwired pins are rnl-std-fill.
A file that wants only this drops rnl-std with an empty inline package of that name in its
header record and uses rnl-std-core there instead (16.3).

name: rnl-std-fill
description:
rnl-std-fill, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std (16.3); it references
rnl-std-virtual. It holds the sets the user edits with ADD-TO and REMOVE-FROM (10.5) and the
fill rules: a ground or supply stub for every unwired pin on a ground or supply net, a port tag
for every port net that has none; the net-name label set and the wire net set are there but
not applied by default. A file that does not want the automatic fill drops this sub-package
with an empty inline package of the same name in its header record (16.3).

name: rnl-std-layout
description:
rnl-std-layout, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std (16.3): the layout definitions
(9.4, 14): a mirrored pair about an axis point, a tail centred under a pair, and signal flow
(14.6).

name: rnl-std-semantics
description:
rnl-std-semantics, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std (16.3): the semantic
definitions (9.4, 9.5, 15.1), roles only, nothing drawn.

name: rnl-std-style
description:
rnl-std-style, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std through rnl-std-core (16.3): the
styles (9.3) and the default style rules, which give every kind of object $base and bus wires
$bus.

name: rnl-std-symbols
description:
rnl-std-symbols, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std through rnl-std-core (16.3):
the symbols of instances (9.2), with the arrow head drawn inside the MOS symbols, and the
rules that give an instance its symbol by element letter, by Spectre master and by model
type. The symbols of the virtual elements are in rnl-std-virtual. Coordinates are y-up; one
unit is one grid step, and pins sit on integer points.

name: rnl-std-virtual
description:
rnl-std-virtual, a sub-package of the standard package rnl-std through rnl-std-core (16.3):
the virtual elements ground, supply, port, no-connect mark, junction and current arrow
(12.5, 12.6, 13.2, 15.2), their symbols and the rules that give their usages these symbols,
and $GND_STUB and $SUPPLY_STUB, a ground or supply right below or above a pin, wired to it
(10.5). rnl-std-fill applies the stubs to unwired pins; without it they can still be applied
by hand. Coordinates are y-up; one unit is one grid step.

name: rnl-std
description:
The standard package rnl-std (standard appendix B, 16.3, U3), used implicitly at the root of
every document. A package collection: it references rnl-std-core, then rnl-std-fill,
rnl-std-semantics and rnl-std-layout, and has no content of its own. Used, it brings them in in
that order, each once (16.2): styles, symbols, virtual elements, fill, semantic and layout
definitions, with the statements and rules of the single file of the RNL toolkit 0.1 in their
order. Its content is a draft: the package of the Python prototype in the research repository
(2026-10-12) with the symbols reviewed, an explicit box= on every symbol (9.2.3), and symbol
rules for Spectre primitives and model cards.

name: rnl-zh
description:
rnl-zh：标准词和标准包名字的中文代称（D16、D17）。由 notes/rnl-vocabulary-brainstorm/terms-zh.md 生成；
标准包的名字（$ 名字和 definition= 的代称）见 terms-zh.md 第九节（2026-10-12 定）。

name: rnl-std-basic
description:
rnl-std-basic 0.3, a package of the standard series 0.3 (16.3).
Generated by build-std.mjs in rnl-dev (notes/analog-canvas-rnl-import-export/std-0.3, 609ab05)
from Analog Canvas 9bbfd340b (packages/components/definitions), symbol-list.json (rnl-dev f0c23b6)
and the hand-written parts there; from here on edited in rnl, whose files are the source.
The symbols of passive parts, sources, switches and transmission lines, of the virtual parts
and the marks; the definitions of the virtual parts and of the parts that are only drawn, the
stubs of ground and supply, and the rules that draw their usages.
Coordinates are y-up; one unit is one grid step, ten Analog Canvas units. Pins bind by terminal
number, so a symbol fits any dialect.

name: rnl-std-structures
description:
rnl-std-structures 0.3, a package of the standard series 0.3 (16.3).
Generated by build-std.mjs in rnl-dev (notes/analog-canvas-rnl-import-export/std-0.3, 609ab05)
from Analog Canvas 9bbfd340b (packages/components/definitions), symbol-list.json (rnl-dev f0c23b6)
and the hand-written parts there; from here on edited in rnl, whose files are the source.
The definitions of circuit structures and of layouts (9.5, 14, 15.1), which rnl-std-semantics and
rnl-std-layout held apart before. Some carry a default drawing in their bodies, whose constraints
are all of priority low (14.8): the author's own facts come before them, PRIORITY("disabled") on a
usage turns them off for that usage, and a rule such as
# @SELECT-USAGE $DIFFERENTIAL_PAIR => @PRIORITY("disabled") for every usage of a definition.
